public_rationale: Using his own measure (revenue from customers outside the disclosed 10%-plus direct customers), the figures hold up. In fiscal Q1 2026, two customers made up 30% of $44.1B, leaving about $30.9B. In fiscal Q3 2026, four customers made up 61% of $57.0B, leaving about $22.2B. That is a fall of about 28% in two quarters, which fairly counts as a collapse on his measure. Two caveats matter. First, these direct customers are mainly server makers and distributors that buy for many end users, so the measure says little about how many companies want NVIDIA chips. Second, some outlets reported four more 10%-plus customers in Q2, which would change his Q2 number but not the Q1-to-Q3 fall.
limitations: Primary 10-Q text could not be read; figures come from reporting that quotes the filings.
The metric is his construction and is sensitive to customers crossing the 10% threshold.
Does not show end-customer diversity fell.

our_interpretation: 'Diversified revenue' is his own measure: total revenue minus revenue from direct customers that each exceed 10% of revenue.
Target period is NVIDIA fiscal Q1-Q3 2026 (late January to October 26, 2025), the quarters he cites.
'Collapsing' read as a large sustained drop over those quarters; a fall of roughly a quarter or more counts.
criteria.support_condition: Revenue outside the disclosed 10%-plus direct customers fell sharply from fiscal Q1 to Q3 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: That revenue was flat or rising across the period, or the disclosed customer shares differ from his figures in a way that removes the decline.
